pr_title: Allow Chacha20-Poly1305 to use a ivlen less than 12 bytes.
pr_body:
Fixes #20084

This is a provider related bug. The generic code to test the ivlen enforces a size of 12 bytes. A special flag was added to allow the generic code to do a different check. i.e. ivlen <= 12 The code to do the zero padding already existed.

A test that does the zero padding was added to a data driven evp_test.

pr_comments: What's the providence of the test vector?
I dont know where to get test vectors for this case (which is why there were none there before).
I am basing the test vector off of the pre existing code non provider code. It will then at least be compatible with what we had pre 3.0

> I am basing the test vector off of the pre existing code non provider code. It will then at least be compatible with what we had pre 3.0

Perhaps we could generate a valid test vector from another cryptography library which supports short IVs?

Putting a OTC hold on this: Do we want to support shorter iv lengths to be backward compatible, (which just left zero pads the iv to 12 bytes and is non standard). Or should it produce an error?
Maybe it should work with padding for 3.0, and error in 3.1 onwards?

> Maybe it should work with padding for 3.0, and error in 3.1 onwards?

IMO no. The 3.0 was the right place where to disable the short nonce support if we decided so. We disabled it inadvertently though. Either we accept that and officially document it, or we fix the code to pad the shorter nonces but then it should be done in all 3.x branches.

> IMO no. The 3.0 was the right place where to disable the short nonce support if we decided so. We disabled it inadvertently though. Either we accept that and officially document it, or we fix the code to pad the shorter nonces but then it should be done in all 3.x branches.

Since we accidentally disabled it anyway and only just now noticed I am tempted to make it official.
I agree. There is no standard requiring/specifying short nonces, so we shouldn't introduce such a standard de-facto.

I also don't see any reason to support short nonces. If it was an official feature of the ChaCha20-Poly1305 RFC that is domain separated from 12-byte nonces that would be one thing, but if it's just a shortcut for zero-padding, and not officially sanctioned at that, I really see no reason to support this, since any application that wants it can just do the padding itself.
The only real reason to do this is for backwards compatibility (it was supported in 1.1.1). But since its broken in 3.0 anyway and has been since it was released we could reasonably not fix it.

**OTC: A different fix is needed. In 3.x fail the CTRL setting an incorrect ivlen. There should be migration-guide and CHANGES entry. In 1.1.1 just update documentation that short IV length just left-pads it with zeros and that it won't be supported in 3.0.**

issue_context.title: ChaCha20-Poly1305 fails to allow you to set a different IV length
comments:
Hmmm...  we essentially have two chacha20-poly1305 implementations, `providers/implementations/ciphers/cipher_chacha20_poly1305.c` and `providers/implementations/ciphers/cipher_chacha20_poly1305_hw.c`.  The former doesn't use the common cipher stuff...  I think? ...  and the latter has its own initiv:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/091f532e0ef57cff71ab710c07eb5f6f9bb88b22/providers/implementations/ciphers/cipher_chacha20_poly1305_hw.c#L76-L105

So I wonder, how did we end up in the generic initiv???

@slontis, might you lend us a hand here?  You have pretty much architected the cipher implementation, so you might know top of your head faster than @mattcaswell and I can dig...

@levitte the *1305poly.c file contains the provider dispatch table. Inside this file it contains a hw pointer used to access common lower level functions.
The _hw.c file  just implements these common set to lower level functions. (For implementations  with multiple platform implementations there are different lower level functions).
Note this code was based of "e_chacha20_poly1305.c" - not off of a deep understanding of the chacha-poly1305 algorithm.
So the nonce_len was already there
In the old e_code it has EVP_CIPH_CUSTOM_IV_LENGTH set as a flag. This is only used by AES and ARIA so I think this is why this happens for this cipher.

We obviously have no test vectors for this case but it basically looks like the counter is always 12 bytes.. The iv just gets left zero padded if it is less than 12.. So a test vector should be fairly easy to do.. I will try adding a custom init instead of using the generic one..

Why do we even support IVs of less than 12 bytes? As far as I can read in all RFCs and documentation about regular ChaCha20-Poly1305 and its use in standard protocols, the nonce/IV is always 12 bytes, and the only mentions of "shorter nonces" is when part of the 12-bytes (usually the first 32-bits) are used as a counter/identifier and the remaining (usually 8) bytes as the only "random" part of the nonce.

https://www.openssl.org/news/secadv/20190306.txt is an example of a security advisory that OpenSSL had to issue because of its nonstandard ChaCha20-Poly1305 behavior. Indeed not covered in the advisory is that, because OpenSSL just pads short nonces up, short nonces of different lengths still collide with each other. A library user less familiar with ChaCha20-Poly1305 might incorrectly assume that OpenSSL's APIs conform to standard AEAD security expectations and use two colliding nonces of different lengths.

If OpenSSL decides to continue with this nonstandard behavior, the documentation should be updated clearly state that its ChaCha20-Poly1305 implementation doesn't conform to the specification and that using incorrect nonce lengths risks nonce reuse where one wouldn't expect it.

Alternatively, OpenSSL can align with the standard and all these issues go away.
